title: Normal coefficient automorphisms conjugate normalized branches without completeness
statement: Let $A\to B$ be an injective local map of discrete valuation rings [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with fraction fields $K\subseteq L$ [def-pc-field-extension]. Let $N/K$ be finite-dimensional and normal, meaning that every irreducible polynomial over $K$ with a root in $N$ splits into linear factors over $N$. Put $E=(L\otimes_KN)_{\mathrm{red}}$, $R=\operatorname{IntCl}_A(N)$ and $C=\operatorname{IntCl}_B(E)$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with reduction the quotient by nilpotents. The group $G=\operatorname{Aut}_K(N)$ acts on $R$ by restriction and on $C$ by restriction of $\sigma(\overline{l\otimes x})=\overline{l\otimes\sigma(x)}$. Its action on the maximal ideals of $C$ is transitive. More precisely, for maximal ideals $q,q'\subset C$ there is $\sigma\in G$ with $\sigma(q)=q'$, and it sends $n=q\cap R$ to $n'=q'\cap R$ and induces a commuting isomorphism of local ring maps $R_n\to C_q$ and $R_{n'}\to C_{q'}$, given on fractions by $b/s\mapsto\sigma(b)/\sigma(s)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. No completeness or henselianity of either DVR, and no separability of $N/K$, is assumed. There is no assertion that $R$ is local or that $n=n'$.

source.place: Tag 09EU (lemma-galois-relative), statement and the orbit-separation proof. In the possibly inseparable case the invariant-power formulation of lem-sfb-normal-tensor-invariant-powers replaces the erroneous fixed-field identity K=N^G in the source proof. Local isomorphisms are the explicit localization of that action.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dvr-algebraic-normalization-structure], case (a), with $P=N$: $E$ is a nonempty finite product of fields, and for every maximal $q\subset C$ its contraction $n=q\cap R$ is maximal and $R_n,C_q$ are DVRs. In particular $E\ne0$. The canonical unital maps $L\to E$ and $N\to E$ have zero kernels, since a proper ideal in a field is zero; we use these inclusions. An $A$-monic equation for $r\in R$ becomes a $B$-monic equation in $E$, so $R\subset C$ by [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Every element of $C$ is integral over $B$ by that definition. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-integral-maximal-contracts-maximal] gives $q\cap B=\mathfrak m_B$ for every maximal $q$, since $B$ is local. Also $B$ is a PID by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], so [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal] says $B$ is integrally closed in $L$.

source.place: Tag 09EU (lemma-galois-relative), proof; finite tensor-normalization setup of Tag 09EM (remark-construction).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-extension-finitely-many-embeddings] with source $N/K$ and target $N/K$, the set of $K$-homomorphisms $N\to N$ is finite; the automorphisms form a subset, so $G$ is finite. For $\sigma\in G$, [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] constructs $1\otimes\sigma$ on $L\otimes_KN$, with inverse $1\otimes\sigma^{-1}$. If $z^a=0$, then $((1\otimes\sigma)z)^a=0$, so this map preserves the nilradical and induces an $L$-automorphism of $E$. Tensor uniqueness gives the identity and composition laws. Applying $\sigma$ to a monic equation over $A$, or the induced map to one over $B$, leaves its coefficients fixed. By [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] these maps restrict to automorphisms of $R$ and $C$, with inverses given by $\sigma^{-1}$. They agree on $R\subset C$ because both send $r$ to the image of $\sigma(r)$. Ring automorphisms carry maximal ideals to maximal ideals: their inverse identifies the quotient rings, preserving the field property.

source.place: Tag 09EU (lemma-galois-relative), proof; finite tensor-normalization setup of Tag 09EM (remark-construction).

proof.text: Suppose two maximal ideals $q,q'\subset C$ lie in different $G$-orbits $O,O'$. These are disjoint finite sets by step 2. Distinct maximal ideals $v,w$ are comaximal: choose $a\in w\setminus v$; the ideal $v+(a)$ strictly contains $v$, hence equals $C$, and is contained in $v+w$. Apply [lem-pc-crt-ideal-quotient-product] to the finite family $O\cup O'$. Its quotient-product isomorphism supplies $b\in C$ with $b\equiv0\pmod v$ for $v\in O$ and $b\equiv1\pmod v$ for $v\in O'$ (choose the corresponding tuple, then a representative in $C$). For $v\in O$, $\sigma^{-1}(v)\in O$, hence $\sigma(b)\in v$. For $v\in O'$, $b-1\in\sigma^{-1}(v)$, hence $\sigma(b)\equiv1\pmod v$. Thus $x=\prod_{\sigma\in G}\sigma(b)$ lies in every ideal of $O$ and is congruent to $1$ modulo every ideal of $O'$. Each $\tau\in G$ fixes $x$, since $\sigma\mapsto\tau\sigma$ permutes the finite product.

source.place: Tag 09EU (lemma-galois-relative), orbit-separating element and product; Chinese remainder is Algebra Tag 00DT (lemma-chinese-remainder), not the mistagged 00U3 in the existing CRT node.

proof.text: View $x\in C$ as an invariant element of $E$. By [lem-sfb-normal-tensor-invariant-powers], applied with its coefficient field $E$ renamed $N$ and its reduced ring renamed $E$, there are $d\ge1$ and $l\in L$ with $x^d=\overline{l\otimes1}$. Because $x^d\in C$, [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] gives a monic equation over $B$ for this element of $E$. The inclusion $L\hookrightarrow E$ from step 1 makes the same equation hold for $l$ in $L$. By the normality of $B$ from [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal], $l\in B$. Now $x\in q$ implies $l=x^d\in q\cap B=\mathfrak m_B$. But $x\equiv1\pmod {q'}$ implies $l=x^d\equiv1\pmod {q'}$, whereas $\mathfrak m_B=q'\cap B\subset q'$. This contradicts $1\notin q'$. Therefore $O=O'$: for arbitrary $q,q'$ there is $\sigma\in G$ with $\sigma(q)=q'$. Only an invariant power is used, never the generally false equality $N^G=K$.

proof.text:
Choose this $\sigma$ and put $n=q\cap R$, $n'=q'\cap R$. For $r\in R$, $\sigma(r)\in n'$ is equivalent to $\sigma(r)\in q'$, to $r\in q$, and to $r\in n$; hence $\sigma(n)=n'$. Use the fraction description of [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The inclusions induce $R_n	o C_q$ and $R_{n'}	o C_{q'}$ by $r/s\mapsto r/s$, since $s
otin n$ implies $s
otin q$. These maps are local: $r/s$ belongs to the extended prime precisely when its numerator does. Indeed a fraction $r/s$ in $pR_p$ can be written $a/t$ with $a\in p$; its equality with $r/s$ gives $u(rt-as)=0$ with $u,s,t
otin p$, so primality forces $r\in p$. The converse is immediate. Applying this for $p=n,q$ shows the preimage of $qC_q$ is $nR_n$, and the same argument works for $n',q'$.

source.place: Tag 09EM (remark-construction), local branch square; explicit fraction and extended-prime calculation using Algebra Tag 00CO (definition-localization).

proof.text: Define $\phi_R:R_n\to R_{n'}$ and $\phi_C:C_q\to C_{q'}$ by $b/s\mapsto\sigma(b)/\sigma(s)$. Denominators stay outside the corresponding primes by $\sigma(n)=n'$ and $\sigma(q)=q'$. If $b/s=b'/s'$, [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] gives $u(bs'-b's)=0$ for some $u$ outside the source prime. Apply $\sigma$ to obtain $\sigma(u)(\sigma(b)\sigma(s')-\sigma(b')\sigma(s))=0$ with $\sigma(u)$ outside the target prime; thus the formula is well defined. The fraction addition and multiplication formulas show it preserves sums, products and $1$. The maps defined using $\sigma^{-1}$ are two-sided inverses on every fraction. The numerator test of step 5 shows these isomorphisms are local. Finally, on $r/s\in R_n$, either route around the square has value $\sigma(r)/\sigma(s)\in C_{q'}$, because the actions agree on $R\subset C$. Thus the square of local ring maps commutes. The argument permits distinct $n,n'$ and uses no completeness, henselianity or separability.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q65-30cdfdf6f (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item in full. It has six steps, no new nodes, and the statement and stmt_deps are identical to the live item. I checked it against Stacks 09EU (lemma-galois-relative), statement and proof. The source's K=(K_1)^G is false for inseparable normal extensions (example: F_p(t^{1/p})/F_p(t), where G is trivial). The report discloses this, and the proof uses lem-sfb-normal-tensor-invariant-powers instead; that node's notion of normal is equivalent to the item's and its action is the same. Step 1: case (a) of the normalization-structure node applies (finite N, injective local map of DVRs). This gives E nonzero, so L and N inject into E. R lies in C. The integral-maximal-contraction leaf gives q∩B=m_B, and the PID-normal leaf makes B normal in L. Step 2: G is finite by the embeddings leaf, which needs no separability. 1⊗σ comes from clauses (2) and (3) of the tensor universal property. Nilradical and integral closures are preserved, and the actions agree on R⊂C. Step 3: the comaximality argument is correct. The CRT node is used only through its isomorphism. Membership of σ(b) in each orbit and the invariance of the product are checked. Step 4: the invariant power x^d is the image of some l in L, and l lies in B. Then l is in m_B, which lies in q', while l≡1 mod q', a contradiction. Nothing is cancelled in the possibly non-domain E. Steps 5 and 6 are elementary from def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime. The numerator test handles annihilators, the localization maps are well defined and local, the inverses come from σ^{-1}, and the square commutes. I tested N=K; Z_(5)[i] over Z_(5), where n≠n' as the item allows; and the purely inseparable and L=N cases. proof_deps equals the union of the uses, and there is no cycle. All inputs are in the same unit sk-thm-sf-ctf-stability or are Mathlib leaves and definitions, so no tool_uses are needed. lem-sfb-epp-normal-base-branch-conjugacy assumes completeness and is not a duplicate. The inherited blueprint chain is preserved. That fault is in the existing node, not this delivery.
